newsitem.title: DENMARK: SALOMON BROS DOWNGRADES TELE DANMARK.
newsitem.headline: SALOMON BROS DOWNGRADES TELE DANMARK.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers on Tuesday downgraded Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark's earnings per share (EPS) expectations for 1997, 1998 and 1999.

Salomon Brothers cited tougher competition, noting that Telia and NetCom are making substantial inroads into the long distance and international segments of the Danish market as reasons for its downgrading.
It also mentioned local rival Sonofon's challenge to Tele Danmark's wired local loop, along with expected major redundancy charges over the three years.

Salomon Brothers cut Tele Danmark's expected EPS for the current year to 13.1 crowns per share from a previous forecast of 20.8 crowns, while 1998's EPS was seen down at 24.6 crowns from a previous estimate of 30 crowns and 1999's EPS was put at 25.7 crowns compared to earlier 32.7 crowns per share.
Tele Danmark's EPS was 23.7 crowns in 1996.
